description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Computing Tools for Translation-Invariant Total Orders' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We introduce TITO_Explore, a software package for representing and computing with Translation-Invariant Total Orders (TITOs). description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Two local zero-sum problems' and formalize its key results. Abstract: In the present paper, we investigate two local zero-sum problems. Let $n,k\ge 2$. We denote by $\mathsf{D}^*(n,nk)$ (resp. $η^{*}(n,nk)$) the smallest positive integer $\ell$ (if exists) such that, from any given $\ell$ integers not divisible by $n$, one can select some (resp. at most $n$) of them whose sum is divisible by $n$ but not by $nk$. description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Two problems on booksize and triangular edges in Nosal graphs' and formalize its key results. B 179 (2026) 219--249] proved that every $m$-edge Nosal graph satisfies $bk(G)> \frac{1}{24}\sqrt{m}$ and $τ(G) > \frac{1}{12}\sqrt{m}$. Recently, Zhai, Li and Lou [arXiv:2601.10163v2] proved that every $m$-edge Nosal graph satisfies $bk(G)> \frac{1}{9}\sqrt{m}$. In this paper, we establish the following result: Every $m$-edge graph $G$ with no isolated vertices and $ρ(G)\geq \sqrt{m}$ that is not isomorphic to any complete bipartite graph satisfies $bk(G)\geq\frac{ρ(G)}{3}$ and $τ(G)\geq ρ(G)$. As direct consequences, we answer a question of Li, Liu and Zhang [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 179 (2026) 219--249] and confirm a conjecture of Li, Feng and Peng [J. Graph Theory 110 (4) (2025) 408--425].

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'On a character-twisted analogue of Schäffer's equation' and formalize its key results. Abstract: Let $f$ be a positive integer, and let $χ$ be a primitive quadratic character of conductor $f$. description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Products of simplices are canonically Ramsey' and formalize its key results. Abstract: A set of points $C \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called canonically Ramsey if there is some set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^{n'}$ such that any colouring of $S$, using any number of colours, must contain either a monochromatic copy of $C$ or a rainbow copy of $C$. Mao, Ozeki, and Wang introduced this notion, showing that 30-60-90 triangles are canonically Ramsey. Since then, various other canonically Ramsey configurations have been identified. The author showed that cuboids are canonically Ramsey, while Ge, Shu, Xu, and Yu recently showed that simplices are canonically Ramsey. We extend both of these results, proving that all products of simplices are canonically Ramsey.

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Certified Optimal Configurations for up to $n\le 8$' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We study Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit right triangle, where $n$ points are placed to maximize the smallest of the $\binom{n}{3}$ triangle areas they span. We prove a boundary-structure result: unless all three vertices are occupied, some optimal configuration with $n \ge 5$ has at least four points on the boundary, one edge carrying two of them. With the affine $S_3$ symmetry this fixes four boundary points and $n$ orientation variables in a mixed-integer model that certifies global optimality for all $n \le 8$, including $n = 7, 8$, where no proof was previously available, closing gaps left by grid search and by branch-and-bound. For $n = 8$ the optimum is conjectured to be the real root of a septic obtained by Chen, Zeng and Zhou, which our reconstruction confirms to $250$ digits. We show its Galois group is $S_7$, so on that conjecture no expression in radicals exists.

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Discrete Einstein metrics on unicyclic graphs' and formalize its key results. Abstract: In earlier work with Cheng and Hua we showed that on a finite tree the discrete Einstein metrics of the Lin--Lu--Yau curvature are the Perron eigenvector of an edge-indexed Ricci matrix. We extend this theory to unicyclic graphs. We determine exactly when the tree picture persists -- the balanced regime, where the spectrum becomes periodic rather than Dirichlet-type -- and compute it in closed form for bare cycles and for regular suns (cycles with pendant leaves); for a single decorated vertex on a long cycle it persists up to an explicit golden-ratio threshold. Beyond this regime the problem is piecewise-linear, and phenomena impossible on a tree appear: the Einstein metric can be non-unique, or absent -- a triangle with a pendant leaf carries none. For the regular suns we prove that it exists and is unique.

Abstract: The Beck--Fiala conjecture asserts that every matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times T}$ with at most $d$ nonzero entries in each column has discrepancy $O(\sqrt d)$. The result is also essentially optimal, since online prefix discrepancy is known to scale as $ω(\sqrt{d})$ for $d =o(\log T)$. As an immediate corollary, the open question of online vector balancing in the Spencer setting is also resolved. The algorithm is based on a compactly supported Metropolis fixed-point walk, constructed by combining ideas from several recent works on the online Komlós problem. description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Aperiodic tile sets from Sturmian lattices' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We give an explicit algorithm to construct aperiodic tile sets based on Sturmian words of quadratic slopes. The method works for any quadratic irrational slope, and we can produce an aperiodic tile set whose underlying scaling constant is a unit of any real quadratic field. There are two key ingredients in our construction. The first one is the ``Sturmian lattices'', an interesting grid structure generated by Sturmian words that emerged in an aperiodic monotile called Smith Turtle. The second is the bounded displacement equivalence of Delone sets, which plays a central role in this construction. A classification of Sturmian lattices and complete proofs are given in the full version.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: Aperiodic tile sets from Sturmian lattices

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'HJ numbers revisited' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We improve the bounds on the Hales-Jewett numbers to a tower of exponentiations. Earlier it was $WaW$ (that is, iterations of towers which are themselves iterated exponentiations). We improve the inductive step there (induction on the size of the alphabet, $|Λ|$) to 2-exponentiations, instead of towers. In the longer work in typing, (A) We present this inductive step as a partition theorem in its own right; (but in this preliminary version we make it just serve the bound on HJ numbers). (B) We shall deal with the density version of Hales-Jewett with similar bound. We are also dealing with the Graham-Rothschild Theorem and the Affine Ramsey Theorem and the polynomial case, and give background.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: HJ numbers revisited

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Robustness of periodicity in Grover walks under a magnetic vector potential' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We study the effect of magnetic vector potentials on periodic Grover walks on finite graphs. The magnetic vector potential is introduced through the framework of quantum graphs, which induces the Grover walk as a special case. We regard the vector potential as a perturbation of a periodic Grover walk and investigate the robustness of its periodicity. Our analysis reveals that the response to such perturbations depends on the spectral structure of the underlying graph. In particular, when the graph possesses at least one non-simple eigenvalue, we derive a Hermitian matrix that characterizes the robustness of its periodicity. As a consequence, we show that the perturbed dynamics is asymptotically described by a continuous-time quantum walk generated by this Hermitian matrix.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: Robustness of periodicity in Grover walks under a magnetic vector potential

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Aperiodicity and subword complexity in the binary expansion of powers of three' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We prove two results on the fine structure of the binary digits of $3^{m}$. First, for every fixed period $p$, the number of positions at which the binary expansion of $3^{m}$ breaks $p$-periodicity grows in order like $\log m/\log\log m$; equivalently, no window of the expansion deeper than a fixed power of $\log m$ is $p$-periodic. Second, the finite binary word formed by the low-order digits of $3^{m}$ has full low-order subword complexity: its complexity function satisfies $\pcx_{3^{m}}(n)\ge n+1$ for every length $n$, once $m$ is large enough.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: Aperiodicity and subword complexity in the binary expansion of powers of three

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Several families of incommensurable noncompact hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We classify all 141 finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter five-dimensional polytopes with eight facets, of which 125 are noncompact. Using maximal-cusp density and a noncompact analog of Bogachev-Douba-Raimbault's argument, we construct infinitely many pairwise incommensurable noncompact Coxeter polytopes in dimensions 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9, with the number of commensurability classes growing at least exponentially in volume.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: Several families of incommensurable noncompact hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes

description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'The Spine: A Supersingular Highway' and formalize its key results. Abstract: We consider the structure of the spine of the supersingular $\ell$-isogeny graph for one of the cases which arXiv:2502.03613 was not able to fully describe, $\ell = 2$ and $p = 71, 119\pmod{120}$. We find the distance, eccentricity, and diameter functions, of the components of the spine without the non-trivial edge not defined over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Using these functions, we find the mean diameter of the spine and show how this value distinguishes the different structures of the spine. Thus, allowing us to use explicit computations to provide heuristics on the behavior of the spine's structure as $p$ varies.
proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
title: ArXiv paper: The Spine: A Supersingular Highway

description: We conjecture that the constant 3 appearing in the threshold (3+o(1))(log n)/(log(1/δ)) for sumset avoidance in δ-dense subsets of [n] is optimal. Specifically, for any fixed δ ∈ (0,1) and any ε > 0, there should exist arbitrarily large n such that every subset S ⊆ [n] with |S| ≥ δn necessarily contains some sumset A+B where A,B ⊆ ℕ satisfy min{|A|,|B|} ≥ (3-ε)(log n)/(log(1/δ)). This would establish that the random construction used in the paper cannot be improved asymptotically.
proof_strategy: The conjecture would likely require a constructive approach or refined probabilistic analysis. One strategy would be to explicitly construct, for each ε > 0, a family of sets S (perhaps deterministic or using altered probability distributions) where every sumset A+B with min{|A|,|B|} ≥ (3-ε)(log n)/(log(1/δ)) must intersect the complement of S. A second approach would use the second moment method or concentration inequalities to show that random sets with density δ cannot avoid all such large sumsets when the threshold drops below 3(log n)/(log(1/δ)).
title: Optimality of the Constant 3 in Dense Sets Without Large Sumsets

description: For every fixed density δ∈(0,1) and every integer t≥2 there is a constant C(t,δ)>0 such that for all sufficiently large n one can find a subset S⊂[n] of size at least δn that contains no t‑fold sumset A₁+⋯+A_t with each |A_i|≥C(t,δ)·(log n)/(log(1/δ))^{1/(t−1)}.  This conjecture generalises the extremal result of Serra‑Szegedy and the recent construction for t=2, and it is compatible with the lower‑bound phenomenon proved by Hernández‑and‑Hetzel.
proof_strategy: Use the probabilistic method: select each element of [n] independently with probability δ to form a random set S.  For any fixed t‑tuple of subsets A₁,…,A_t ⊂ ℕ with |A_i| ≥ C·(log n)/(log(1/δ))^{1/(t−1)}, the sumset A₁+⋯+A_t is a set of size at least exp(Ω(log n)) = n^{Ω(1)} in the worst case.  A Chernoff bound shows that the probability that all these sum‑elements lie outside S is at most exp(−Ω(δ·|A₁+⋯+A_t|)).  A union bound over all such t‑tuples (there are at most n^{tC(log n)/(log(1/δ))}) keeps the failure probability bounded away from 1 if C is chosen small enough.  Thus with positive probability S satisfies the desired property, proving existence.  A deterministic construction could be obtained by the method of conditional expectations.
title: Existence of Dense Sets without Large t‑Fold Sumsets

description: For any fixed δ ∈ (0,1) and sufficiently large n, there exists a subset S ⊂ [n] with |S| ≥ δn such that no A, B ⊂ ℕ with min{|A|,|B|} ≥ (3+o(1)) log n / log(1/δ) satisfy A+B ⊂ S.

description: For every integer k ≥ 5, there exists a constant C_k > 0 such that for a uniformly random simple k-regular graph G on n vertices (with n → ∞ through admissible values), with probability tending to 1, G satisfies the following asymptotic Brill-Noether existence property at half-canonical degree: for every integer r ≥ 0 with ρ(g, r, g-1) ≥ 0 (where g = n(k/2 - 1) + 1 is the genus of G), there exists a divisor D on G of degree at most C_k(g-1) and rank at least r/C_k. proof_strategy: The proof follows the paper's approach: (1) Establish a Cheeger-style inequality relating the covering radius of the Jacobian lattice (periodic set) with respect to the energy quadratic form to the spectral gap of the graph. (2) Show that random k-regular graphs for k ≥ 5 are expanders with high probability, giving a uniform spectral gap. (3) Use the Cheeger inequality to bound the covering radius, which implies the existence of divisors with the required degree and rank bounds via Minkowski's theorem or lattice point counting in the Jacobian. (4) Translate the covering radius bound into the asymptotic Brill-Noether statement using the geometry of numbers framework developed in the paper.

# Future directions

This development formalizes the finite coordinate core of Curtin's *Generalizations of nets and Latin squares* (arXiv:2607.10890v1): column- and row-Latin matrices, orthogonality, cooperative pairs and systems, coordinate reticulations, svelte arrays, unique cross-line intersections, the grid-coordinate characterizations of Lemma 7.5, and the `m*n` cardinality consequence of Theorem 3.1.

Natural next steps are:

1. **Partition-level incidence structures.** Connect the coordinate-fibre representation here to a literal structure whose lines are finite sets and whose families are `Set.PairwiseDisjoint` covers. Prove both representations equivalent, including all seven clauses of Theorem 3.1.
2. **Full inverse correspondence.** Package the maps between ordered reticulations, svelte semi-orthogonal arrays, and normalized cooperative systems as equivalences, proving Theorems 6.2, 6.3, 7.7, and 7.8 at structure level rather than only the forward encodings established here.
3. **Multiplicity and foundations.** Model multisets of line families, then formalize repetition-free reticulations and Proposition 4.1.
4. **Parastrophy and isotopy.** Define the permutation actions from Sections 9 and 10 and prove that they preserve the cooperative and reticulation axioms.
5. **Constructions.** Formalize prolongation, splicing, and direct products from Sections 12–14, with formulas for their parameters.
6. **Classical specializations.** Build translations from nets, mixed orthogonal arrays, mutually orthogonal Latin squares, and bireversible Mealy automata, recovering Propositions 3.6 and 6.6 and Theorem 7.3.
7. **Finite search.** Add executable enumeration of small repetition-free systems up to isotopy, together with kernel-checked certificates for any reported counts.

# Future Directions: Minimal Modularity Lifting for Genus Two

## 1. Integral stable-Yoshida modularity lifting

Let a four-dimensional residual symplectic representation arise by automorphic induction from a nearly ordinary Hilbert modular eigencuspform over a real quadratic field. Under minimal ramification and the standard residual irreducibility and regularity conditions, the universal minimal ordinary deformation ring should be isomorphic, integrally and not merely after inverting the residue characteristic, to the localized genus-two ordinary Hecke algebra.

**The key insight is...** the stable Yoshida description should turn the residual four-dimensional problem into a controlled two-dimensional deformation problem while preserving the symplectic polarization needed on the Siegel side.

**Why now?** The algebraic consequences of such an isomorphism—transport of points, uniqueness, and freeness—can be treated uniformly, so the remaining task is sharply localized in the arithmetic construction and patching argument.

## 2. Two-variable finite-flat strengthening

In the stable-Yoshida minimal setting, the universal ordinary deformation ring should be finite flat, and generically étale, over the two-variable Iwasawa weight algebra; moreover, its rank should equal the multiplicity of the corresponding ordinary Hecke component.

**The key insight is...** freeness should reflect a constant arithmetic multiplicity across weight space, while generic étaleness should follow from the vanishing of the relevant adjoint Selmer obstruction at a Zariski-dense set of classical points.

**Why now?** Freeness is already naturally transported by the `R = T` identification, leaving rank and ramification as concrete invariants that can falsify or refine the conjecture.

## 3. Rigidity beyond very regular weights

Uniqueness of an ordinary Hida family through a stable-Yoshida genus-two eigenform should continue to hold at all noncritical cohomological weights, with failure occurring precisely on an explicitly describable congruence or endoscopic locus.

**The key insight is...** uniqueness is fundamentally a statement about the local degree and reducedness of the weight map, rather than about a particular numerical regularity bound.

**Why now?** The abstract uniqueness mechanism identifies surjectivity and local ring structure as the decisive inputs, suggesting a direct investigation of the exact boundary where regularity can be weakened.

## 4. Companion-family stratification

When uniqueness fails at a critical or congruence point, the number of ordinary genus-two families through that point should be governed by the dimension of an ordinary adjoint Selmer group, with tangent directions partitioned according to refinements of the local crystalline representation.

**The key insight is...** distinct families agreeing at one classical eigensystem should be detected infinitesimally by the kernel of the tangent map from the deformation space to weight space.

**Why now?** The uniqueness theorem has a precise algebraic failure mode—loss of effective surjective control—so tangent-space calculations offer a falsifiable explanation for every additional branch.

## 5. Higher-degree Yoshida-type induction

For suitable totally real extensions and polarized nearly ordinary Hilbert modular forms, automorphic induction should yield analogous minimal modularity lifting theorems for higher-genus symplectic groups, with one Iwasawa variable for each independent ordinary weight direction.

**The key insight is...** the transport consequences of `R = T` are independent of genus; only the construction of the comparison map, local deformation conditions, and automorphy input change.

**Why now?** The separation of formal commutative algebra from arithmetic hypotheses provides a stable template against which higher-rank proposals can be tested without conflating universal consequences with genus-specific arguments.

# Future Directions: Quantum Surreal Observation

## 1. Finite-dimensional non-Archimedean spectral calculus

**Conjecture.** Let an ordered non-Archimedean real-closed field carry a standard-part map on its finite elements, and let its quadratic extension play the role of complex scalars. Every self-adjoint matrix whose entries and eigenvalues are finite admits an orthogonal spectral decomposition, and taking standard parts intertwines this decomposition with the ordinary real or complex spectral decomposition whenever distinct eigenvalue clusters remain appreciably separated.

The key insight is that appreciable spectral gaps should prevent infinitesimal perturbations from merging eigenspaces under standard part.

**Why now?** Finite Born normalization and infinitesimal branch collapse isolate exactly the algebraic and boundedness hypotheses needed to test this claim first for two-by-two matrices, before introducing infinite-dimensional completeness.

## 2. Support equivalence under Maslov dequantization

**Conjecture.** For every finite hyperreal probability vector with finite logarithmic rates, the support surviving standard-part observation equals the zero-level argmax set of its Maslov-dequantized tropical weights, after normalization by the largest rate.

The key insight is that standard part detects appreciable scale, while tropicalization records the leading asymptotic scale; both should select precisely those coordinates that are not exponentially suppressed.

**Why now?** The reservoir theorem proves this equivalence for a Dirac-shaped penalty model and identifies the observable-dependent dominance condition that a general formulation must preserve.

## 3. Quantitative stability threshold for tropical and additive observations

**Conjecture.** Given a finite infinitesimal probability model and a tropical penalty vector, there is a sharp oscillation threshold for observables below which ordinary standard-part expectation and tropical maximization select the same exposed face of the outcome simplex. Beyond that threshold, every disagreement pattern compatible with the supports can occur.

The key insight is that the inequality `f(i) + M_i ≤ f(r)` is not merely sufficient: its boundary should form the normal fan separating stable support agreement from visible-outcome escape.

**Why now?** The finite reservoir bridge supplies one complete cone of this fan and shows explicitly why unconditional agreement is false.

## 4. Standard-part projection-valued measures

**Conjecture.** A finite hyperreal projection-valued measure with finite matrix entries descends under entrywise standard part to an ordinary projection-valued measure if and only if its projections are pairwise orthogonal up to infinitesimal operator norm and its total projection is infinitesimally close to the identity.

The key insight is that polynomial identities defining projections and orthogonality should survive standard part, while approximate hypotheses capture the natural measurement errors of non-Archimedean states.

**Why now?** Scalar standard-part normalization and support collapse are established; the next falsifiable step is to determine exactly which matrix identities survive observation.

## 5. Infinite-dimensional boundary of the spectral conjecture

**Conjecture.** On a spherically complete non-Archimedean Hilbert space, every compact self-adjoint operator with appreciably separated nonzero spectrum has an orthogonal eigen-expansion whose standard part agrees with the spectral expansion of the descended compact operator; without spherical completeness, a counterexample exists.

The key insight is that the obstruction is expected to lie in completeness and convergence, not in the finite algebraic spectral identities.

**Why now?** Separating the finite matrix theorem from this completeness-sensitive extension turns the broad spectral claim into two independently testable stages and supplies a precise failure mode to seek.

# Future Directions

## 1. Certified finite-prefix null tests for π, e, and √2

Fix a prefix length in advance and compare centered decimal-digit autocorrelations at lags 1–12 against the exact permutation distribution, with family-wise error controlled across constants and lags. The conjecture is that none of the three advertised preferred lags remains significant after correction at prefix lengths 10³, 10⁴, and 10⁵.

The key insight is that an exact finite-sample null distribution separates reproducible digit evidence from interpretations based only on irrationality. Why now? The deterministic energy identity identifies the precise statistic to test and exposes every convention that must be fixed before significance has a meaning.

## 2. Temporal-lag and pitch-interval separation

Define a pitch-interval histogram counting pairs whose digit values differ by a prescribed number of semitones, independently of their temporal separation. Under the stated ten-note chromatic map, the conjecture is that octave counts are identically zero, while any temporal lag-12 effect is unrelated to octave incidence.

The key insight is that sequence position and pitch distance are orthogonal coordinates and should never share the word “lag.” Why now? The present analysis shows that the original octave interpretation is structurally incompatible with a digit alphabet of width ten.

## 3. Fourier-energy characterization of digit-melody repetition

For centered cyclic digit prefixes, the conjecture is that statistically exceptional autocorrelation peaks are equivalent to concentration of Fourier power on characters whose phases nearly stabilize the corresponding shift, with quantitative two-sided bounds uniform in prefix length.

The key insight is that Fourier inversion turns temporal repetition into spectral concentration, while polarization turns it into low interval energy. Why now? These two exact descriptions are now available in one framework, making a sharp stability theorem a concrete target.

## 4. Continued fractions versus decimal consonance under controlled ensembles

Compare numbers sampled from bounded-partial-quotient Cantor sets with matched control samples, using a pre-registered consonance functional on decimal prefixes. The conjecture is that, after conditioning on prefix length and digit frequencies, bounded partial quotients do not produce a universal positive consonance bias.

The key insight is that continued-fraction digits and decimal digits arise from different dynamical codings; any bridge between them must be measured against a controlled ensemble rather than inferred from isolated constants. Why now? The failure of irrationality alone to constrain finite autocorrelation narrows the search to genuinely dynamical mechanisms.

## 5. Prefix-prescription obstruction theorem

For every finite decimal word and every prescribed finite vector of lag correlations compatible with that word, construct both a transcendental real and a quadratic irrational sharing the word whenever the algebraic class permits the same prefix. The conjecture is that no statistic depending on a fixed finite prefix can distinguish transcendence from algebraicity with certainty.

The key insight is that finite musical data constrain an interval of real numbers, not the arithmetic nature of an individual tail. Why now? This obstruction would give a rigorous boundary for all attempts to infer deep arithmetic properties from finite sonifications.

## What was established

The formal development proves a general finite-tag amplification theorem. Relative to an abstract provability predicate, one dark existential predicate yields dark predicates with 1, 2, 3, and in fact every positive finite number of distinct tagged witnesses. The tagged coding is proved to enumerate every tag over every originally named object. It also proves that any named witness-extraction principle rules darkness out.

This gives a concrete obstruction to the proposed strict hierarchy: witness count alone is not an invariant measure of proof-theoretic hardness. Irrelevant finite tags amplify the level without adding mathematical information.

## Important correction to the mission framing

Paris–Harrington and Kirby–Paris hydra independence do not by themselves instantiate the definition given in the prompt. Their usual statements are universal termination/finite combinatorics claims independent of PA, whereas the proposed definition requires PA to prove an existential while proving no numeral instance. An explicit PA example therefore needs a carefully fixed arithmetization of syntax, a naming map, and a nonstandard or intensional predicate; it cannot be inferred merely by citing those independence theorems.

Likewise, “dense in the space of Pi_2 statements” is undefined until a topology or asymptotic density on formula codes is selected. Raw counting of formulas is coding-dependent: harmless syntactic padding can arbitrarily change frequencies. Any meaningful density theorem should first prove robustness under acceptable changes of Gödel numbering.

## Next formal targets

1. Instantiate `Prov` with a concrete arithmetized first-order proof calculus for PA and prove `SupportsFiniteTagging` by primitive-recursive transformations of proof codes.
2. Investigate whether a genuine dark predicate exists under the exact external reading of `PA ⊬ T(n)`. Compare this with the numerical existence property and witness properties of fragments such as HA and constructive arithmetic.
3. Define an equivalence relation identifying predicates that differ only by finite tags or primitive-recursive bijections, then seek a hierarchy on equivalence classes.

# Future directions

The formal result in `AffineDuality.lean` isolates a precise bridge between finite-group symmetry and cryptographic proof systems: translation gives exact witness-independent transcript distributions, while subtraction extracts a witness from two accepting answers sharing a commitment.

## 1. Move from transcript multisets to probability distributions

The current theorem represents uniform finite sampling by the multiset obtained from `Finset.univ`. A natural next step is to restate perfect zero knowledge as equality of `PMF` values. This would make composition with randomized verifiers and repeated protocols more direct.

## 2. Sequential and parallel repetition

Formalize `k` independent Boolean challenges. The expected goals are:

- simulated and real transcript vectors have identical distributions;
- witness independence is preserved by product distributions;
- if a cheating prover can answer both challenges at any repeated coordinate, subtraction extracts a witness;
- under a suitable binding or fixed-commitment hypothesis, the soundness error decreases exponentially.

The last point cannot follow from the present algebraic model alone: it needs an explicit probabilistic adversary model and assumptions preventing challenge-dependent commitments.

## 3. Connect to propositional proof verification

Encode a propositional derivation as a finite list of locally checkable steps. A commitment layer can then hide the list while a verifier asks for selected local consistency checks. The important formal distinction is between:

- local consistency of sampled steps;
- global soundness of the encoded proof;
- zero knowledge of the resulting transcript.

A one-step opening protocol by itself does not establish the latter two properties. A rigorous development should use a sound locally testable encoding and a hiding, binding commitment scheme.

## 4. Replace the abstract additive relation by concrete protocols

Instantiate the construction with finite cyclic groups and linear maps, then connect it to Schnorr-style identification. This requires carefully separating additive notation in the exponent from multiplicative notation in the public group.

## 5. Computational and communication complexity

The present development is information-theoretic and extensional; it does not claim polynomial communication in the statement length. A future complexity-aware formalization should represent algorithms, encodings, security parameters, and bit lengths explicitly. Any PA-wide succinctness claim must account for proof length and use a genuinely succinct argument system rather than infer statement-length communication directly from arithmetization or the PCP theorem.

## 6. Malicious-verifier zero knowledge

The simulator currently captures the fixed-challenge, honest-verifier view. General zero knowledge requires quantification over verifier strategies and simulation of their complete views. Formalizing rewinding, expected running time, or straight-line simulation would clarify exactly which privacy guarantee survives beyond honest verifiers.

# Future Directions: Recurrence in Cognitive Dynamics

## 1. Observation-invariant recurrence spectra

**Conjecture.** For compact metric cognitive systems related by a topological conjugacy, the exact-period spectrum, topological entropy, and existence of Li–Yorke scrambled sets are simultaneously invariant; under a merely finite-to-one observation map, exact periods can only decrease by divisibility.

The key insight is that faithful semiconjugacy already preserves exact period pointwise, while loss of injectivity is the precise mechanism by which an observed cycle can collapse. **Why now?** The finite-state embedding and exact-period transport results isolate the hypotheses needed to extend recurrence invariance from individual states to global entropy and chaos.

## 2. Measured recurrence instead of point density

**Conjecture.** In a parametrized family of cognitive observation models, lifetime recurrence incidence is determined by the measure of an observation-thickened recurrent set, not by the cardinality or topological density of periodic points; the two quantities can vary independently even among maps with dense periodic points.

The key insight is that population incidence is probabilistic, whereas density of periodic points is topological and carries no canonical percentage. **Why now?** The contraction counterexample rules out continuity as a sufficient explanation, and the faithful-observation theorem supplies a principled way to state how measurement changes recurrence.

## 3. Period-three forcing with cognitive observability

**Conjecture.** Let a continuous interval map have an exact period-three orbit and let an observation map separate the three orbit states by a fixed positive margin. Then there is a quantitative lower bound, depending only on that margin and a modulus of continuity, for the number of distinguishable finite observation words of length `n`, growing exponentially in `n`.

The key insight is that period three should force symbolic complexity only when the observation process can distinguish the forced orbit structure. **Why now?** Exact period three has been converted into an explicit three-state embedding, making quantitative separation the natural next hypothesis rather than an implicit assumption.

## 4. Logistic parameter windows and robust recurrence

**Conjecture.** Near the parameter `r = 3.83`, the logistic family admits an open parameter interval with an attracting exact three-cycle whose basin has positive Lebesgue measure, while the fixed-point set remains measure zero throughout that interval.

The key insight is that robust observed recurrence should be modeled through basin measure and attraction, not through the density of the periodic points themselves. **Why now?** The exact fixed states and critical value at `3.83` are known algebraically, so the remaining problem is a falsifiable stability and basin-measure calculation.

## 5. Tropical drift as a recurrence obstruction

**Conjecture.** For an irreducible min-plus cognitive transition matrix, a tropical eigenstate is periodic in the ordinary state space exactly when its eigenvalue is zero; modulo additive constants, every tropical eigenstate is fixed, and eventual projective recurrence is governed by the cyclicity of the critical graph.

The key insight is that a tropical eigenvalue records linear drift, so quotienting by global activation offset separates genuine recurrence from uniform translation. **Why now?** Zero-eigenvalue recurrence and the full iterate drift formula are already established, leaving critical-graph cyclicity as the concrete bridge from tropical spectral theory to periodic cognition.

# Future directions

## What the formal result establishes

`Catalog/Computation/SoundOfPi.lean` audits the proposed digit-to-note model before undertaking statistical tests.  With pitch offset equal to the decimal digit, every generated note lies between 0 and 9 semitones above the base frequency.  Thus any two generated notes are at most 9 semitones apart, and no generated pair can be an octave (12 semitones) apart.  A repeated digit at temporal lag 12 is instead a unison.  This distinction is independent of which real number supplies the digits.

## Necessary corrections to the research hypothesis

1. **Separate temporal and pitch lags.** Autocorrelation at sequence lag 12 compares digit positions twelve time steps apart; it does not measure a twelve-semitone interval. To study musical intervals, use the distribution of `|dᵢ - dⱼ|` (or pitch classes modulo 12) for a clearly specified pair of positions.
2. **Choose a map capable of octaves.** The proposed map has only offsets 0–9. An octave statistic requires either a larger alphabet, octave registers, or another mapping whose image contains pitches 12 semitones apart.
3. **Specify autocorrelation.** State whether digits are centered, which finite prefix is used, and whether the statistic is Pearson autocorrelation, equality frequency, or another quantity. These are not equivalent.
4. **Pre-register significance tests.** Testing 13 lags for three constants creates multiple-comparison issues. Give the null model, sample size, test statistic, correction, and significance threshold in advance.
5. **Do not infer infinite-digit laws from finite prefixes.** A significant finite-prefix statistic would be empirical evidence about that prefix, not a theorem about π, e, or √2. Irrationality only rules out eventually periodic decimal expansions; it does not imply normality or a particular autocorrelation law.
6. **Clarify the continued-fraction claim.** π and e do not have bounded partial quotients established by the proposal, while √2 does. A theorem connecting decimal digit consonance to continued-fraction coefficients would require a precise statistic and substantial new number theory.

## Next formal developments

* Define finite digit words and exact equality counts at lag `ℓ`.
* Prove general bounds `0 ≤ count ≤ N - ℓ` and identify lag-zero behavior.
* Define interval histograms separately from temporal autocorrelation.
* Encode supplied finite decimal prefixes as certified data and prove their exact count tables by kernel-checked computation.
* Formalize the elementary theorem that an eventually periodic base-10 expansion represents a rational number, then use known irrationality results to obtain non-eventual-periodicity for π, e, and √2 where library support permits.
* Only after the statistic and data are fixed, formalize rational-valued chi-squared calculations and their assumptions.

No claim of a statistically significant preference is made here because the request provides neither a prefix length nor digit data nor a precise statistic and null test.

# Future Directions: Quantum States with Non-Archimedean Probabilities

## 1. Standard-part Born measures on arbitrary finite supports

**Conjecture.** Let a finitely supported state have finite hyperreal amplitudes and appreciable nonzero squared norm. Then taking the standard part of every normalized Born weight produces a nonnegative real probability distribution of total mass one. Its support is exactly the set of branches whose normalized weights are appreciable and have positive standard part.

The key insight is that standard part should commute with finite sums once all summands are finite, while appreciability of the norm prevents normalization from magnifying an infinitesimal numerator into a visible weight.

**Why now?** Normalization and the disappearance of one infinitesimal branch have been established separately; the finite-support theorem would unify them into a complete measurement law.

## 2. Observational equivalence as a quotient of non-Archimedean state space

**Conjecture.** For appreciably normalized finite states, equality of all standard-part Born probabilities defines an equivalence relation compatible with relabelling and with tensoring by an appreciably normalized ancillary state. The quotient admits a canonical map to the simplex of real probability distributions.

The key insight is that infinitesimal perturbations of amplitudes can change exact hyperreal weights without changing any observed probability, suggesting that observation is naturally a quotient rather than an injective representation.

**Why now?** The equal-amplitude and infinitesimal-amplitude results isolate both sides of this equivalence: ket labels alone do not alter probabilities, whereas infinitesimal changes can disappear under observation.

## 3. A finite-dimensional spectral theorem over a real-closed non-Archimedean field

**Conjecture.** Every symmetric matrix over a real-closed non-Archimedean ordered field is orthogonally diagonalizable after passing to the field's algebraic real closure, and every finite eigenvalue has a standard-part eigenvalue satisfying the characteristic polynomial of the entrywise standard-part matrix, under a uniform finiteness hypothesis.

The key insight is that the algebraic spectral theorem and the standard-part map address different layers: diagonalization is controlled by real closedness, while observational eigenvalues require finiteness and compatibility of standard part with polynomial evaluation.

**Why now?** The present measurement model is diagonal in a fixed surreal-indexed basis. A matrix theorem is the next testable step toward genuine observables without prematurely asserting an infinite-dimensional spectral theorem.

## 4. Dirac collapse for finite lexicographic probability towers

**Conjecture.** Replace pairs of rationals by finite lexicographic towers `ℚ^(k+1)`. Successively projecting away the last coordinate yields a filtration of observations, and an event first becomes visible precisely at the earliest coordinate where its mass is nonzero. Every normalized nonnegative finite measure therefore determines a hierarchy of real-valued shadow measures.

The key insight is that the first-coordinate standard part proved here is the first stage of a general valuation-like filtration, not an isolated construction.

**Why now?** The two-coordinate model already exhibits exact normalization, finite additivity, and collapse to a Dirac measure; finite towers provide a concrete setting in which higher-order infinitesimal visibility can be tested.

## 5. Tensor-product stability of infinitesimal invisibility

**Conjecture.** If a branch in one appreciably normalized finite state has infinitesimal amplitude, then every product branch containing it has zero observed probability after tensoring with any finite state whose squared norm is finite and appreciable. Conversely, tensoring two appreciable branches preserves positive observed weight whenever both standard-part weights are positive.

The key insight is that product amplitudes multiply and standard part is multiplicative on finite hyperreals, so invisibility should form a tensor ideal among branches.

**Why now?** Single-state invisibility is known, but compositional stability is essential before the model can represent composite systems or independent experiments.
title: **Conjecture.** Let a finitely supported state have finite hyperreal amplitudes

# Future Directions

## Result established

`Catalog/Applications/HyperbolicNumberTheory/CayleyPythagoreanBridge.lean` gives a precise replacement for the underspecified “hyperbolic integers” proposal. For the integer-translation subgroup of the modular group, it studies the Cayley image

\[
z_n=\frac{n}{n+2i}.
\]

It proves simultaneously that:

1. every `z_n` lies strictly inside the Poincaré disk;
2. the orbit lies on the horocycle `|2z_n-1|²=1`, tangent to the ideal boundary at `1`;
3. clearing the horocycle equation produces the integral right-triangle identity
   \[(n^2-4)^2+(4n)^2=(n^2+4)^2.\]

This is the connector: a modular cusp orbit in hyperbolic geometry and Euclid-style Pythagorean triples are two realizations of one circle equation.

## Natural formal extensions

1. **Primitivity classification.** Prove an exact formula for
   `gcd (n² - 4) (4n)` and classify when the resulting Pythagorean triple is primitive after normalization.
2. **Rational parametrization equivalence.** Show that every rational point on the horocycle except its tangency point comes from a unique rational parameter, then identify integral modular parameters as a distinguished discrete subset.
3. **Hyperbolic metric formulation.** Add the Poincaré distance and prove the exact distance of `z_n` from the origin, relating cusp escape to logarithmic growth in `|n|`.
4. **General cusp width.** Replace `2i` by a positive integral width and derive the corresponding family
   `(n²-w², 2wn, n²+w²)`.
5. **Matrix-level modular action.** Represent translations by determinant-one matrices, prove compatibility of the Cayley transform with their Möbius action, and connect the horocycle equation directly to the parabolic trace condition.
6. **Counting theorem.** Count orbit points below a Euclidean or hyperbolic radial cutoff and compare the resulting one-dimensional cusp law with ambient hyperbolic area growth.
7. **Primitive geodesics and Selberg zeta.** A meaningful prime theory should use primitive hyperbolic conjugacy classes (closed geodesics), not arbitrary tessellation vertices. Formalizing this requires definitions of primitive classes, lengths, and the Selberg zeta product before any prime-geodesic or zero statement can be posed.

## Scope boundaries

The original proposed `Z_H`, multiplication, prime vertices, norm, and zeta series are not specified well enough to support unique factorization, a prime number theorem, or a zero computation. In particular, tessellation vertices do not automatically inherit a canonical multiplicative monoid, and a claim about “the first 100 zeros” requires a precise analytic function, continuation, zero ordering, and certified numerical enclosures. None of those conjectural claims is asserted here. The proved connector instead uses canonical data from the modular translation orbit and makes no unverified spectral claim.

# Future directions

## What the formal development establishes

The original proposal mixes two different notions. The files now separate them.

1. In `Pythagorean/EscherStaircases.lean`, an ascending chain indexed by `ℕ` has
   intersection equal to its first term:

   \[
   I_0 \subseteq I_1 \subseteq I_2 \subseteq \cdots
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
   \bigcap_n I_n=I_0.
   \]

   Moreover, zero belongs to every ideal and hence to every intersection of ideals.
   Thus merely requiring the intersection to contain zero does not define an
   additional “looping” phenomenon.

2. The proposed divisibility family has the containment direction reversed.
   Divisibility by `2^(n+1)` is stronger than divisibility by `2^n`. The ideals
   `(2^n)` in `ℤ` are proved to form a strictly descending chain with zero
   intersection. `Catalog/Algebra/EscherDivisibilityDisproof.lean` proves the same
   strict reversal for the pointwise divisibility ideals in the function ring
   `ℤ → ℤ`.

3. `Catalog/Algebra/EscherStaircase.lean` adopts the coherent replacement

   \[
   \operatorname{EscherStaircase}(R)
   \;:\!\!\Longleftrightarrow\;
   \exists I:\mathbb N\to\operatorname{Ideal}(R),\; I\text{ is strictly increasing}.
   \]

   It proves that this is equivalent to failure of `IsNoetherianRing`. It also
   constructs an explicit staircase in the product ring `ℕ → ℤ`, beginning at the
   zero ideal, and proves that the p-adic integers admit no such staircase.

4. `Catalog/Algebra/EscherStaircasePolynomial.lean` constructs the strict chain

   \[
   (0) \subsetneq (x_0) \subsetneq (x_0,x_1) \subsetneq \cdots
   \]

   in the countably generated polynomial ring. Its strictness is certified by a
   specialization homomorphism that kills the old variables but not the new one.
   The file concludes that this polynomial ring is not Noetherian.

5. `Catalog/Algebra/EscherStaircaseHilbert.lean` proves the complementary Hilbert
   basis results: polynomial rings in finitely many variables over a field, and the
   ordinary univariate polynomial ring, admit no Escher staircase. It packages this
   with the countably generated example as a finite/countable-variable dichotomy.

These results are complete Lean proofs. They do **not** establish a numerical
“Escher height”: under the coherent existence definition, the invariant is a
Noetherian/non-Noetherian dichotomy rather than Krull dimension.

## Status of the original examples

### Integer-valued polynomials

For

\[
J_n=\{f\in\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb Z):f(\mathbb Z)\subseteq 2^n\mathbb Z\},
\]

one has `J_(n+1) ⊆ J_n`, not the reverse. Constant polynomials witness strictness:
the constant `2^n` belongs to `J_n` but not to `J_(n+1)`. Consequently this family
cannot witness failure of the ascending chain condition. A direct Lean construction
of `Int(ℤ)` remains worthwhile, but it would formalize a descending filtration, not
the claimed ascending staircase.

### Finitely many polynomial variables

For a field `k`, `k[x₁,…,xₙ]` is Noetherian, so it has no infinite strictly
ascending chain of ideals. Its Krull dimension is `n`, but that is a separate
invariant defined using chains of prime ideals. Calling this number an Escher height
would require a new definition and proofs that the definition agrees with Krull
dimension.

### All algebraic integers

The requested numerical height is not currently well-defined. A meaningful future
project should first choose one of the established invariants below and only then
study the ring of all algebraic integers.

## Concrete continuation projects

1. **Formalize integer-valued polynomials.** Define `Int(ℤ)` as the subring of
   `ℚ[X]` whose elements take integral values on integers. Define the value-
   divisibility ideals, prove they are antitone and strictly decreasing using
   constants, and prove their intersection is zero by evaluation and polynomial
   extensionality.

2. **Develop Krull dimension independently.** Use strict chains of prime ideals and
   connect finite-variable polynomial rings to the standard dimension theorem. This
   is the mathematically appropriate interpretation of the number of variables.

3. **Study adic separation.** For an ideal `I`, investigate `⋂ n, I^n = 0`. The
   formalized powers-of-two theorem is the elementary model. General continuations
   include separated filtrations and Krull-intersection hypotheses.

4. **Generalize explicit non-Noetherian witnesses.** Extend the variable-ideal
   construction from a countable variable set to arbitrary infinite index types,
   extracting a countable sequence of distinct variables under suitable choice or
   embedding assumptions.

5. **Analyze algebraic integers with a precise target.** Possible targets include
   explicit ascending chains witnessing non-Noetherianity, prime-ideal chains for
   Krull dimension, or descending valuation filtrations. These should not be merged
   into one invariant without a theorem relating them.

The formal development therefore resolves the logical inconsistency in the original
staircase and supplies rigorous replacements: failure of ACC for ascending chains,
Krull dimension for prime chains, and adic separation for descending powers.
title: The original proposal mixes two different notions. The files now separate them.

## What is proved now

`Heegner163.lean` gives a kernel-checked elementary chain connecting Euler's
quadratic polynomial to the discriminants 43, 67, and 163. It proves the sharp
prime runs, the exact discriminant calculations, the exact cube-plus-744 integer
identities, their modular consequences, and that 163 is the maximum of the

## Highest-priority missing mathematics

1. **Do not treat the proposed uniqueness statement as established.** The claim

# Future Directions: A Periodic Table of Finite Groups

## 1. Extension fingerprints refine composition columns

**Conjecture.** Among groups of order at most 2000, the multiset of composition factors together with the directed incidence data of complemented chief factors separates substantially more isomorphism classes than composition factors together with derived length and nilpotency class.

The key insight is that the order-six collision is caused not by missing factor sizes, but by missing information about how factors act on one another. A compact extension fingerprint should therefore be a more chemically meaningful “valence shell” than a single integer.

**Why now?** The factor-ledger obstruction precisely identifies what the first axis remembers and the order-six example isolates the smallest missing interaction. This makes a finite, falsifiable census comparison possible.

## 2. Solvability is the maximal robust composition-factor property

**Conjecture.** For finite groups, every property determined solely by the multiset of composition factors and invariant under replacing each solvable factor by another cyclic factor of the same prime order factors through the dichotomy “all factors are cyclic of prime order” versus “at least one factor is nonabelian simple.”

The key insight is that solvability genuinely belongs to composition-factor chemistry, whereas commutativity, nilpotency, derived length, and automorphism-group order depend on extension data.

**Why now?** The present obstruction cleanly separates factor data from multiplication data, allowing the boundary of composition-determined properties to be formulated rather than inferred from isolated examples.

## 3. Minimal extension data for square-free atomic numbers

**Conjecture.** For groups of square-free order, the composition-factor multiset together with the action graph whose arrows record nontrivial conjugation actions determines the isomorphism type.

The key insight is that all composition factors then have distinct prime orders, so multiplicity ambiguities disappear and the remaining chemistry should be encoded by which prime-order layers act on which others.

**Why now?** Atomic number six shows exactly one nontrivial action distinguishes the cyclic and symmetric cases. Square-free orders offer the next broad family in which this mechanism can be tested without repeated-factor complications.

## 4. A predictive bound from action complexity to derived length

**Conjecture.** There is a universal function bounding the derived length of a finite solvable group by the height and maximum strongly connected component size of a suitably defined chief-factor action graph; for square-free order, the bound can be taken to be one plus the longest directed path.

The key insight is that derived length is not visible in the factor ledger, but each commutator layer should require a chain of nontrivial actions between factor layers.

**Why now?** Replacing the failed one-column periodic law with a two-axis model suggests a quantitative prediction rather than merely a classification label.

## 5. Information-theoretic optimality of periodic-table invariants

**Conjecture.** Any invariant that distinguishes all finite groups of order at most `N` must encode asymptotically more information than the prime-factor ledger and any bounded list of scalar invariants; an extension-action encoding can achieve this lower bound up to a polynomial factor in description length.

The key insight is that the enormous number of groups at prime-power orders arises from extension choices invisible to composition factors, so classification can be viewed as a compression problem constrained by group cohomology.

**Why now?** The smallest collision already proves that scalar chemistry is lossy. A census up to 2000 can compare concrete encoding lengths and expose which structural descriptors scale with the true diversity of groups.

# Future Directions: Tropical Hashing Beyond Coordinate Minima

## 1. Complexity transition under coupled message constraints

Conjecture: If messages are restricted by a sparse system of integer difference constraints and the output must equal a prescribed value, tropical preimage existence exhibits a dichotomy governed by the constraint graph: it is polynomial-time decidable on bounded-treewidth graphs and NP-complete on unrestricted graphs.

The key insight is that the unconstrained fiber has a complete coordinatewise certificate, so any genuine hardness must arise from coupling the coordinates rather than from the tropical minimum itself.

Why now? The exact fiber characterization isolates the inequalities and active equality that a constraint system must interact with, making both dynamic programming and hardness reductions sharply testable.

## 2. Universal collisions for finitely many tropical keys

Conjecture: For an `r`-component hash formed from `r` independent min-plus linear forms on `k` real coordinates, every message has an unbounded collision ray whenever `k > r`.

The key insight is that each component needs only one unchanged minimizing coordinate; after choosing at most `r` such witnesses, any remaining coordinate can be increased without changing any output component.

Why now? The two-key theorem proves the first nontrivial case and supplies the exact update lemma needed for an induction over an arbitrary finite key family.

## 3. Geometry and dimension of generic fibers

Conjecture: For generic `r`-key data with `k > r`, every nonempty fiber is a finite polyhedral complex whose maximal cells have dimension at least `k-r`, with equality on a dense set of attainable outputs.

The key insight is that a tropical fiber is cut out by ordinary linear inequalities together with a disjunction of active-coordinate equalities, while simultaneous keys intersect these unions in a controlled polyhedral arrangement.

Why now? Exact single-key fiber certificates and deterministic collision directions identify both the cells and their recession directions, reducing the conjecture to a finite active-set analysis.

## 4. Collision resistance from nonlinear tropical circuits

Conjecture: There exist bounded-depth tropical circuits with coordinate mixing and a discrete message alphabet for which finding collisions is average-case hard under a standard combinatorial assumption, whereas every fixed number of uncoupled min-plus linear forms remains collision-rich.

The key insight is that adding independent linear keys does not create diffusion: security requires nonlinear reuse and coupling of coordinates, not merely more coordinatewise minima.

Why now? The universal two-key collision theorem gives a rigorous obstruction that candidate constructions must escape and suggests a precise design test: every input coordinate must influence active witnesses through multiple coupled layers.

## 5. Mining thresholds and recession cones

Conjecture: For tropical circuits whose acceptance region is defined by output thresholds, mining difficulty is controlled by the recession cone of the corresponding polyhedral complex; finite expected search requires the nonce trajectory to avoid every nontrivial recession direction.

The key insight is that the proven coordinate update is a recession direction of a hash fiber, so unrestricted nonce motion can produce entire rays of equivalent candidates rather than pseudorandom trials.

Why now? The collision construction supplies an explicit recession direction, while the concavity bridge links tropical evaluation to the geometry needed to classify threshold regions.

# Future Directions

## What the formal result establishes

The proposed “interval topology” is the ordinary order topology: open intervals and open rays generate the same topology on a linear order. The formal development shows that this topology on Mathlib’s universe-relative `Surreal` type is **totally separated**, hence totally disconnected and not connected. It also proves:

- every path in `Surreal` is constant;
- `Surreal` is not path connected and not contractible;
- nevertheless, the fundamental group at every basepoint is trivial.

The last point is the connector: trivial fundamental group does not imply contractibility. Here it follows for the opposite reason from the proposed one—there are no nonconstant loops because there are no nonconstant paths at all.

## Why density and “no gaps” do not prove connectedness

Order density alone is insufficient. The rational line is densely ordered but disconnected. For a linear order with its order topology, connectedness requires a strong order-completeness condition in addition to density. Surreal numbers have a different obstruction: their non-Archimedean hierarchy creates clopen additive cuts.

Given `x < y`, the proof constructs a positive surreal `ε` such that

`n ε < y - x`

for every natural number `n`. The set

`{z | ∃ n : ℕ, z < x + n ε}`

is both open and closed, contains `x`, and excludes `y`. This separates every pair of distinct points.

## Proper-class caveat

Lean cannot place a literal proper class inside its ordinary type theory. Mathlib’s `Surreal.{u}` is a universe-relative type of numeric pre-games modulo equivalence. The key boundedness theorem applies to families whose index type is small relative to that universe. The connector theorem is therefore a precise theorem about each such universe-relative surreal line. A class-topological treatment of Conway’s full `No` would require an explicit theory of large/class-indexed topologies and should not silently be identified with ordinary set-based topology.

## Local compactness

The statement “every point has a neighborhood basis of intervals with surreal endpoints” is a statement about the order topology, not local compactness. Local compactness additionally requires compact neighborhoods. A future development should characterize compact intervals in universe-relative `Surreal` and determine whether any nontrivial compact neighborhoods exist. One promising route is to use the clopen finite-step cuts to construct open covers of candidate intervals with no finite subcover.

## Stronger algebraic-topological consequences

Since every continuous map from a connected space to `Surreal` is constant, one can aim to formalize:

1. every map from a sphere `Sⁿ` to `Surreal` is constant;
2. all positive-dimensional homotopy groups are trivial at every basepoint;
3. singular simplices in positive degree are constant, leading to vanishing reduced singular homology in positive degrees;
4. path components are singletons while connected components are also singletons.

These results would sharpen the distinction between weak algebraic invariants and global contractibility: all based homotopy groups may vanish even though the space is highly disconnected and noncontractible.

## Alternative topologies

A genuinely connected topology on surreal numbers, if desired, cannot be the topology generated by ordinary order intervals. Future work could investigate:

- coarse class topologies not induced by the linear order;
- topologies on bounded-birthday strata and their direct-limit behavior;
- quotient or valuation topologies that collapse non-Archimedean scale cuts;
- whether field operations remain continuous under any such connected topology.

Any uniqueness conjecture should first specify the class/set framework, separation axioms, continuity of field operations, and the exact meaning of completeness and local compactness for a proper class.
title: The proposed “interval topology” is the ordinary order topology: open intervals

# Future Directions: Computable Shadows of Chaotic Dynamics

## 1. Certified shadowing from cone-field data

**Conjecture.** A program implementing a differentiable map on a compact invariant set, together with machine-checkable stable/unstable cone bounds and a uniform local rounding certificate, admits a computable horizon-independent shadowing radius. The radius should be extractable from the cone expansion, contraction, angle separation, and rounding constants.

The key insight is that a raw Lipschitz estimate records only worst-case expansion, whereas hyperbolic cone data records the directional cancellation that makes classical shadowing possible.

**Why now?** The finite-horizon geometric estimate isolates exactly the step that loses uniformity, so the missing directional structure and the constants it must replace are explicit and testable.

## 2. Backward-error semantics for floating-point chaotic programs

**Conjecture.** For a specified IEEE-754 implementation of a polynomial dynamical system, every finite execution avoiding overflow and exceptional values can be translated into an exact real pseudo-orbit whose local defect is bounded by a compositional expression in unit roundoff and the intermediate magnitudes.

The key insight is that floating-point execution should first be interpreted as a certified pseudo-orbit; only then should a dynamical shadowing theorem be applied.

**Why now?** The abstract pseudo-orbit theorem already consumes precisely such a local defect certificate, leaving a sharply delimited semantics problem rather than an informal appeal to “precision.”

## 3. Adaptive logistic-map shadowing beyond the global factor four

**Conjecture.** For pseudo-orbits of the parameter-four logistic map that remain a certified distance from the critical point, a product of local derivative envelopes yields an exponentially smaller shadowing budget than the uniform factor `4^N`, and this adaptive budget is asymptotically sharp on periodic itineraries.

The key insight is that the interval-wide Lipschitz constant four discards orbit information; local derivative products retain the actual itinerary-dependent amplification.

**Why now?** Forward invariance and the global certificate are established, providing a baseline against which a local, itinerary-sensitive refinement can be quantitatively compared.

## 4. Residual networks as nonautonomous shadowing systems

**Conjecture.** A depth-varying residual system `x ↦ x + g_n(x)` with certified constants `L_n` admits a pseudo-orbit bound governed by products of `(1+L_n)`, and under a summability or averaged contraction condition this bound becomes uniform in depth.

The key insight is that residual robustness and numerical shadowing are instances of the same nonautonomous error recurrence, but varying layers permit stability mechanisms invisible in a single worst-case constant.

**Why now?** The autonomous residual bridge identifies the common calculus; the next test is whether layerwise structure can convert a geometric finite-depth estimate into a uniform guarantee.

## 5. Polynomial shadowing horizons from quantitative hyperbolicity

**Conjecture.** For computable uniformly hyperbolic maps with rational cone certificates, the maximum certifiable shadowing horizon at fixed tolerance grows at least polynomially in the reciprocal local defect when all certificate arithmetic is performed at logarithmic precision.

The key insight is that dynamical existence, numerical conditioning, and computational complexity must be controlled simultaneously; none alone establishes a feasible shadowing algorithm.

**Why now?** The current geometric bound exposes an exponential obstruction for continuity-only arguments, making quantitative hyperbolicity the natural candidate mechanism for a polynomial complexity law.

# Future Directions

## Formal conclusions

The file `Speculative/MoebiusArithmetic.lean` separates the topology from the proposed arithmetic and proves the following.

### Disproved

1. **Coordinatewise operations induce a ring on the Möbius quotient.** Both coordinatewise multiplication and coordinatewise addition fail the representative-independence test. For multiplication, applying the twist to both representatives reverses the fiber sign twice, while the quotient gluing reverses it only once. Thus there is no induced operation of the stated kind, so the advertised zero-divisor calculation does not establish a ring or a failure of integral-domain structure.

2. **The formula embeds an integer as the real number it claims to represent.** For every positive integer `n`, the represented value
   `|n| * (2 * (1/2 + 1/(2n)) - 1)` is `1`; for every negative integer it is `-1`. The coordinate pairs for `2` and `3` remain distinct, but the claimed real-number interpretation collapses them.

3. **`-1` is a prime encoding orientation.** In the ordinary integer arithmetic recovered by the factorization formulas, `-1` is a unit and therefore is not prime.

4. **`-6 = (-2)(-3)`.** This is false: the right side is `6`. The corrected equality is `-6 = 2 * 3 * (-1)`.

5. **Zero has a prime factorization.** A finite product of nonzero integer factors is nonzero, so zero has no such factorization.

### Proved

* The endpoint relation used here is an equivalence relation and identifies `(0,y)` with `(1,-y)`.
* `6 = 2 * 3` and `-6 = 2 * 3 * (-1)`.
* The only integer units are `1` and `-1`, clarifying that orientation behaves like a unit rather than a prime in standard factorization.

## Promising corrected research programs

1. **Transport a ring structure through an explicit bijection.** One can place a ring structure on a bare set underlying a quotient only after constructing a bijection with a known ring. Such a structure would generally not be coordinatewise and would need a separate geometric naturality criterion.

2. **Use a ring bundle rather than a ring on total-space points.** A Möbius line bundle supports fiberwise addition, but multiplication of two twisted fibers naturally lands in the tensor square, which is an untwisted line bundle. A graded algebra containing both twisted and untwisted sectors may encode the “two twists cancel” law faithfully.

3. **Study orientation as a unit or grading.** The algebraic analog of orientation is naturally an order-two unit or a `Z/2Z` degree. Group rings, crossed products, and graded rings are more suitable than declaring orientation prime.

4. **Repair the integer embedding.** Specify independently whether the goal is an injective discrete subset of the band, a compactification of the integers, or a map whose scalar evaluation equals `n`. The displayed formula cannot simultaneously provide the claimed scalar value and compactification behavior.

5. **Formalize the actual quotient topology.** The present development proves the algebraic obstruction at the setoid level. A later development could use Mathlib quotient-topology APIs to establish topological properties, after first correcting the proposed subset and its accumulation point.

# Future Directions: Moonshine Products and Character Reconstruction

## 1. Class-indexed pole order for the Monster

Construct the 194 normalized McKay–Thompson series in a common analytic setting and prove that their class-indexed product has a pole of exact order 194 at the infinite cusp, with no cancellation in its leading coefficient. This sharply distinguishes a product over conjugacy classes from a product over group elements.

**The key insight is...** normalized principal parts aggregate additively under finite products, so the indexing convention leaves an observable signature in the pole order.

**Why now?** Exact class tables and replicable formulas provide finite input data, while the algebraic factorization theorem identifies the single analytic condition—control of the regular factors—needed to lift the result to genuine series.

## 2. Minimal compensator for positive weight

Determine whether there is a canonical meromorphic compensator whose product with all class-indexed McKay–Thompson functions transforms with a prescribed positive weight, and classify the smallest possible divisor of such a compensator on the relevant modular curve.

**The key insight is...** a finite product of weight-zero invariant functions remains weight zero; therefore every nonzero weight must come from an additional factor, multiplier system, or altered operation.

**Why now?** The weight obstruction isolates a precise repair of the proposed positive-weight product and turns an inconsistent transformation claim into a concrete divisor-minimization problem.

## 3. Finite coefficient threshold for character recovery

Find the least integer `N` such that the coefficient functions through degree `N` of the 194 McKay–Thompson series uniquely recover every irreducible Monster character and the multiplicities of all graded pieces determined up to that degree. A falsifying outcome would be two distinct nonnegative multiplicity tables with identical classwise traces through degree `N`.

**The key insight is...** recovery is an injectivity problem for a truncated character-evaluation operator, and positivity plus integrality may force injectivity substantially earlier than unrestricted linear algebra predicts.

**Why now?** The abstract reconstruction theorem identifies injectivity as the exact boundary, making ranks, integral kernels, and positivity cones of finite truncations directly testable.

## 4. Analytic finite-product theorem across levels

For a finite family of meromorphic modular functions attached to possibly different finite-index subgroups, prove that their product is meromorphic modular of weight zero for the intersection subgroup, and determine its complete cusp divisor from the individual cusp divisors. Apply the theorem to every McKay–Thompson family for which compatible expansions are available.

**The key insight is...** finite products do not create a convergence problem once the factors are meromorphic; the genuine issues are the common symmetry group, cusp compatibility, and divisor bookkeeping.

**Why now?** The algebraic product law already controls principal exponents, so the next extension has a sharply delimited analytic and geometric scope rather than requiring an unspecified global convergence argument.

## 5. Information loss beyond the character table

Test whether the complete family of McKay–Thompson series determines subgroup data such as maximal-subgroup conjugacy classes, or whether nonisomorphic finite groups can share equivalent graded character data while having different subgroup lattices.

**The key insight is...** an injective character table recovers class functions and representation multiplicities, but subgroup incidence is additional structure and need not be encoded by character values alone.

**Why now?** Separating what character evaluation provably reconstructs from stronger group-theoretic claims supplies a falsifiable boundary for the assertion that a q-expansion determines “every property” of a group.
title: Construct the 194 normalized McKay–Thompson series in a common analytic setting

# Dark Mathematics — results and future directions

## Formal results

`Tropical/DarkMathematics.lean` treats provability as an abstract predicate `Pr : Prop → Prop` with the minimal rule that provability is preserved by valid implication. It proves:

1. **Level 1 equals ordinary darkness.** The proposed base definition and the one-witness version coincide.
2. **The proposed strict hierarchy collapses.** From any dark predicate `T`, tagging a hidden witness by `Fin k` constructs a level-`k` dark predicate for every finite `k`. Thus levels 1, 2, and 3 require no successively stronger independence principles. On a fixed predicate, level `l` implies every lower level `k ≤ l`.
3. **Dark predicates are exactly an incompleteness phenomenon in the relevant sense.** They cannot occur for semantic truth, in a theory with the numerical existence property, or when the theory is sound and complete for the instances under consideration.
4. **Canonical construction from an undecided sentence.** If a theory proves `U ∨ ¬U` but proves neither `U` nor `¬U`, the Boolean predicate selecting those alternatives is dark. Tagging it produces every finite level.
5. **Provable concrete instances refute darkness.** Any family with even one provable named instance fails the definition.

These statements are kernel-checked and contain no `sorry` or added axioms.

## Disproved or unsupported mission claims

### The strict level hierarchy is false as stated

Counting distinct witnesses does not measure proof-theoretic strength when the predicate's domain may change. The formal tagging construction sends a witness `x` to the distinct pairs `(i,x)`, one for each `i : Fin k`, while each tagged assertion is definitionally just `T x`. A strict hierarchy would need restrictions preventing such coding, plus a precise reducibility or strength relation.

### Paris–Harrington and hydra do not directly provide the requested dark predicates

Their standard independence statements concern a universal assertion (or totality) not provable in PA. Each fixed finite Paris–Harrington instance and each fixed finite hydra computation is, in the ordinary setup, finitely checkable and provable in PA. Therefore indexing the usual finite instances gives the opposite of condition (2). The formal theorem `provable_instance_refutes_dark` captures this obstruction.

### “Dense” and “most” are not defined by counting formulas

The collection of syntactic Pi-2 sentences is countable. Density requires a topology, and “most” requires a measure or an asymptotic-density convention together with a fixed Gödel numbering and length model. Raw counting is presentation-dependent: harmless recodings and padding can alter syntactic frequencies without changing mathematical content. Consequently the density conjecture has no invariant theorem statement yet and was not silently replaced by a weaker claim.

### This is a form of incompleteness

The split construction turns any sentence independent of a classical theory into a dark existential over `Bool`. It therefore shows that the definition repackages undecidability/incompleteness rather than separating a new phenomenon from incompleteness.

## Promising corrected questions

1. Fix a recursively axiomatized theory, an explicit arithmetized proof predicate, a formula class, and a computable numbering; then formalize the abstract results for that syntax.
2. Prohibit witness tagging by fixing the domain and a natural equivalence/reducibility relation. Ask whether levels separate under many-one or interpretability reductions.
3. Replace “density” by a specified model: prefix-free program-size density, bounded Gödel-code density, or Baire-category notions on completions of a theory. Prove invariance results before interpreting any proportion.
4. Investigate constructive theories with existence properties. The proved `no_dark_of_numericalExistenceProperty` theorem predicts that the original notion disappears there.
5. For Paris–Harrington or hydra, study dark predicates built from undecidable *global bounds* or consistency statements, not from their concrete finite instances. Any such construction must prove both formalized PA-provability of the existential and PA-unprovability of every named instance.
